heading: INT. WITCH'S TOWER - TOP CHAMBER - NIGHT

units.text: INT. WITCH'S TOWER - TOP CHAMBER - NIGHT
A round room of grey stone, windows shuttered against a gale.
Shelves of jars, bundled herbs, an iron cauldron cold on its hook.
A single candle in a bottle.
On a table, a roll of parchment sealed with black wax.
WITCH IOLANTHE (70s, long white hair, moth-eaten shawl, bare feet) lowers herself onto a stool by the table.
She stares at the parchment for a long time.
She doesn't touch it.
Well. Don't be a coward.
units.name: IOLANTHE

units.text: She cracks the seal with her thumbnail.
The wax pops loose.
The parchment unrolls itself like a tongue.
A small silver bell falls out and rings once on the stone.
She picks up the parchment.
Her lips move as she reads, and then a voice, her own, young and clear, speaks from the page.
"Dear Iolanthe, if you are reading this, the winter was long, and I am afraid I am not coming back. I left the tower to you because no one else could climb it."
units.name: IOLANTHE

units.text: Iolanthe sets the parchment on her knee.
She laughs, short and dry.
You always had a flair for drama.
units.name: IOLANTHE

units.text: She goes to the shutter and cracks it.
Wind rushes in, sending the candle flame dancing.
Beyond the glass the black sea of the forest tosses below.
"The cauldron needs oil. The raven eats only on Thursdays. And do not, whatever you do, open the third door."
units.name: IOLANTHE

units.text: Iolanthe frowns.
She looks at the iron door in the far wall.
It has been boarded over, rusted, nails bent.
Third door. Third door.
units.name: IOLANTHE

units.text: She crosses the room.
Presses her palm against the wood.
Cold.
She exhales, takes the bell from the floor, and sets it on a shelf where it catches the candlelight.
"But if you must, then know that I have not left you alone. Ring the bell three times, and let the room answer."
units.name: IOLANTHE

units.text: Iolanthe lifts the bell.
Studies it.
She glances at the boarded door.
Absolutely not.
units.name: IOLANTHE

units.text: She sets the bell down.
The wind knocks at the shutter.
She closes it, latching it with a firm hand, and returns to the stool.
The parchment is still open on her knee.
One last line glows at the bottom, in her own handwriting.
"I am only asking you to be brave once."
units.name: IOLANTHE

units.text: Iolanthe's shoulders drop.
For a while she sits, breathing.
Then she rises, goes to the shelf, picks up the bell, and holds it out at arm's length.
Fine.
units.name: IOLANTHE

units.text: She rings it once.
Twice.
Her hand shakes.
She lowers it for the third.
She rings it.
Behind her the nails in the boarded door begin to slide out, one by one, ringing on the stone.
She doesn't turn around.
She sets the bell down on the table, picks up the candle in its bottle, and walks toward the door.
